newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-CORINTHIANS ONE POINT FROM SAO PAULO TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CORINTHIANS ONE POINT FROM SAO PAULO TITLE.

text.p: Corinthians and Sao Paulo won rough, bad-tempered matches at the weekend and will meet on Thursday to decide the Sao Paulo championship.
Corinthians beat crisis-torn Palmeiras 2-0 on Sunday as both players had a man sent off while Sao Paulo beat 10-man Santos 1-0 with a controversial penalty.

Corinthians fans fought a running battle with police on the terraces near the end of their game, but no arrests or injuries were reported. Witnesses said trouble began when police attempted to tear down a banner bearing the name of the banned supporters' group known as "Hawks of the Faithful."
Sao Paulo and Corinthians have each won their two games in the four-team final stage, where the teams play each other once.

If Thursday's decisive match ends in a draw, Corinthians will take the title on having the better overall record in the tournament. Palmeiras, who sacked coach Marcio Araujo last Tuesday one month after giving the job on a full-time basis, will meet Santos in a meaningless game the same day.

Palmeiras, with Araujo originally employed on an interim basis, enjoyed a 16-match unbeaten run at the start of the tournament but fell apart after injuries to key defender Cleber and striker Viola. Luizao, Viola's striking partner, was sold to Spain's Deportivo Coruna last month.
Corinthians central defender Henrique headed Corinthians in front in first half injury time and striker Mirandinha wrapped up the game early in the second half.

Palmeiras defender Vagner and Corinthians midfielder Silvinho were dismissed in the first half for second bookable offences but the red card tally could have been much higher as numerous vicious fouls went unpunished.

Santos were livid at having midfielder Baiano sent off in the first half against Sao Paulo and also felt short-changed by the penalty from which Dodo, the competition's topscorer with 19 goals, won the game midway through the second half.

Dodo, the revelation of the tournament, did not appear to be touched as he tussled for the ball with defender Narciso but went tumbling over anyway in another uncompromising encounter where a tolerant referee kept the red cards down to one.
Neither of the weekend's main games in the Rio de Janeiro championship took place.

The Rio football federation on Tuesday had accepted a request from Vasco da Gama to suspend the games until the national team returns home from its tour to Europe and the Copa America at the end of the month.
As a result the Flamengo v Vasco and Fluminense v Botafogo games, which will decide the third stage winners, were postponed to undisclosed dates.

Flamengo said on Wednesday they would abandon the discredited tournament but the next day, in what appeared to be a show of strength, the Rio federation scheduled Flamengo's outstanding fixture away to Americano for June 4.
Americano beat Bangu 2-1 in the tournament's only game at the weekend. The fixture was almost completely ignored by the media and public alike.
